name: Wind
description: Air that moves, a gentle draft that never stays still.
reason: Two masses of air can combine into a moving mass, which we call wind.

name: Soil
description: Two piles of earth pressed together become a richer, usable ground.
reason: Two piles of dirt together become a richer, usable ground.

name: Campfire
description: Two fires side‑by‑side merge into one, steady blaze that warms and cooks.
reason: Two fires next to each other naturally form what people call a campfire.

name: Lake
description: A wide, still body of water that stretches across the meadow, reflecting the sky like a silver mirror. Its surface is smooth, broken only by the occasional ripple from a passing breeze.
reason: Two bodies of water combine to form a larger body of water.

name: Airplane
description: A metal machine that flies by pushing against air. It carries people and cargo across skies.
reason: A metal aircraft uses air to generate lift and fly.

name: Dust
description: Tiny, dry grains that cling to everything when the wind lifts a mud splash. It settles on boots, shelves, and the underside of a freshly brewed tea pot, as if the air itself is a polite housekeeper.
reason: Air naturally lifts and disperses the fine particles that make up mud, turning them into dust.
